title: The Unreliable Map
text:
Postmodern fiction often refuses to offer the reader a stable center. Instead of a single authoritative narrator, a novel may present several contradictory accounts, each one undermining the others. The reader is left to assemble a meaning that never fully settles into place.

Critics have described this technique as a form of playful skepticism toward grand narratives. By exposing the fragility of its own structure, the text invites us to question how any story, including history, acquires its authority. Such ambiguity, however, is not merely decorative; it reflects a deep unease about the reliability of language itself.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what does postmodern fiction often refuse to offer?
How do critics describe the technique mentioned in the second paragraph?
options: a form of playful skepticism toward grand narratives
a traditional way to build suspense
a simple record of historical events
an attempt to flatter the reader

questions.text: What can be inferred about the effect of the text on its reader?
options: It encourages the reader to question how authority in stories is established
It convinces the reader that history is always accurate
It asks the reader to accept one narrator's version of events
It makes the reader lose interest in the role of language

questions.text: Why does the author describe ambiguity as 'not merely decorative'?
options: Because it reveals doubt about whether language can be fully reliable
Because it shows that the writer prefers simple ornamentation
Because it proves that all narrators are honest
Because it makes the structure of the text easier to follow

vocabulary.definition: firm and not likely to change or collapse
saying or showing opposite things at the same time
a habit of doubting claims that are generally accepted
the quality of having more than one possible meaning

paragraph_translations: Постмодерністська проза часто відмовляється пропонувати читачеві стійкий центр. Замість одного авторитетного оповідача роман може подавати кілька суперечливих версій, кожна з яких підриває інші. Читач мусить сам скласти значення, яке ніколи повністю не встановлюється на місце.

Критики описують цей прийом як форму грайливого скепсису щодо великих наративів. Викриваючи крихкість власної структури, текст спонукає нас запитувати, як будь-яка історія, включно з історією, набуває авторитету. Проте така неоднозначність не є лише декоративною; вона відображає глибоку тривогу щодо надійності самої мови.
